question: A rollout uses minReadySeconds=60. New pods have been Ready for 15 seconds; old replicas remain and no errors appear.
A: Wait for the availability interval before judging rollout failure.
B: Treat Ready replicas as immediately available and delete old replicas.
rubric: Ready is not Available until minReadySeconds elapses.

question: A pod requests 2 CPU. A node has 4 allocatable CPU, 3 already requested, and actual usage 0.4 CPU. Scheduler reports insufficient CPU.
A: Free or resize CPU requests, or add allocatable capacity.
B: Reduce actual CPU utilization without changing requests or capacity.
rubric: Scheduling uses requests against allocatable capacity.

question: A Service selects two pods. EndpointSlice lists only one ready endpoint; the other pod is Running but readiness fails. Requests reach only one pod.
A: Change the Service selector to include the Running pod before investigating probes.
B: Investigate the failing readiness probe before changing Service selectors.
rubric: Running does not imply ready; the selector already matches both.

question: A pod tolerates a NoSchedule taint but has required node affinity for zone A; all available nodes are zone B.
A: Add another toleration to make zone B nodes eligible.
B: Resolve required node affinity or provide eligible zone A capacity.
rubric: Tolerations do not override required affinity.

question: A build copies package manifests then runs npm ci, then copies source. Only source changes and dependency layer is cached.
A: Keep dependency caching and inspect the later source build step.
B: Invalidate dependency caching because every source edit changes the manifest layer.
rubric: Earlier layers remain reusable when their inputs are unchanged.

question: A container uses --memory=512m and reports OOMKilled=true; host has 20 GB free.
A: Inspect container memory usage against its cgroup limit.
B: Increase host free memory without changing the container limit.
rubric: Container limit can trigger OOM despite host headroom.

question: A container publishes 8080:80. The process listens on 127.0.0.1:80 inside the container; host requests fail while container loopback works.
A: Publish another host port while retaining the loopback-only listener.
B: Bind the process to an appropriate container interface.
rubric: Port publishing cannot reach a loopback-only listener via container IP.

question: A bind mount over /app hides files baked into the image; removing the mount reveals them.
A: Rebuild the image to restore files while retaining the same masking mount.
B: Inspect the host mount contents and destination.
rubric: Bind mount obscures image contents at its destination.

question: A pipeline stashes files on agent A and later uses agent B with an empty workspace; no unstash step exists.
A: Unstash the artifacts on agent B before consuming them.
B: Retry the consumer on agent B without transferring artifacts.
rubric: Stash requires explicit unstash in the destination workspace.

question: A parallel stage writes two branches to the same shared output path; each passes alone but concurrent runs corrupt files.
A: Isolate branch output paths or synchronize shared writes.
B: Increase parallelism while retaining the shared output path.
rubric: Concurrent writes explain interference.

question: A shell script runs tests piped to tee; shell lacks pipefail and tee exits zero while tests exit nonzero.
A: Treat the successful tee exit as proof that tests passed.
B: Preserve the test exit status using suitable shell handling.
rubric: Pipeline status can be the last command status.

question: A build is queued with label linux-arm; idle agents all have label linux-x86 only.
A: Increase executors on agents that still lack the required label.
B: Provide a matching agent or correct the label requirement.
rubric: Executor availability does not satisfy label constraints.

question: df -h shows free blocks but df -i shows zero free inodes; creating a tiny file fails ENOSPC.
A: Free inodes or expand inode capacity where supported.
B: Free only data blocks while leaving inode exhaustion unchanged.
rubric: File creation needs an inode.

question: A systemd service reads an environment file at startup; file was edited but process environment is unchanged.
A: Restart the service safely to read the new environment.
B: Run daemon-reload alone and expect existing process environment to change.
rubric: Existing process environment does not update from file edits.

question: df shows filesystem full; du totals much less; lsof shows a large deleted file held open by a process.
A: Delete the already unlinked pathname again to reclaim its blocks.
B: Arrange safe release of the open deleted file.
rubric: Blocks remain allocated until final open reference closes.

question: Load average is high, CPU mostly idle, many tasks in uninterruptible sleep, storage latency elevated.
A: Treat load average as direct proof of CPU saturation.
B: Investigate blocked I/O and storage latency.
rubric: Linux load includes uninterruptible tasks.

question: An IAM role allows s3:GetObject but a bucket policy explicitly denies the same principal and object; no exceptions match.
A: Resolve the applicable explicit deny through authorized policy review.
B: Add another identity allow for the same denied request.
rubric: Explicit deny overrides allow.

question: An ALB target group health check uses /health on port 8080; app serves /ready on 8080 and /health returns 404; matcher is 200.
A: Align health check path with the intended readiness endpoint.
B: Increase target capacity while retaining the failing health path.
rubric: Health matcher rejects 404.

question: An EC2 instance in a private subnet has route to NAT gateway; NAT public subnet lacks route to internet gateway.
A: Add another private subnet NAT route while leaving NAT egress broken.
B: Restore the required public subnet internet gateway route.
rubric: Public NAT needs internet gateway connectivity.

question: A security group permits inbound HTTPS; subnet NACL permits inbound 443 but denies outbound ephemeral response ports. TCP handshake fails.
A: Add another inbound security group rule without fixing NACL return path.
B: Review stateless NACL return-path rules.
rubric: NACL is stateless and must allow return traffic.
